clue.text: A dry slippery character recalled ex-PM

parts.note: TT, teetotal, describes someone who stays off drink, so dry

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the word for the slippery creature runs backwards

parts.note: an eel is the proverbially slippery creature

explanation.surface: Someone drily recalls a slippery former prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns EEL into LEE. Clement Attlee was the Labour prime minister from 1945 to 1951.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement Attlee led Britain's post-war Labour government, so he is a former prime minister.

clue.text: A tale about hypocrisy in Spanish place

indicators.note: about means around, so the tale's letters surround the hypocrisy

parts.note: a tale can be a lie, a made-up story
cant is hypocritical, pious talk

explanation.surface: A story involving pretence is set in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container. Alicante is a port on Spain's Costa Blanca.
explanation.definitionFit: Alicante is a Mediterranean city and province on Spain's east coast.

clue.text: It is used to settle court action

definitions.text: It is used to settle court action

parts.words: It is used to settle court action
parts.note: the court is a tennis court rather than a law court, and the settling decides a level set

explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, a set tied at six games each is decided by this special deciding game.

clue.text: Nervous journalist disheartened guy

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

indicators.note: disheartened means losing the heart, the middle letter, keeping only the first and last

explanation.surface: A jittery reporter has lost his nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' leaves the first and last letters of GUY.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on edge is the state of being tense and jumpy, which is what nervous describes.

clue.text: Harsh son, one inspired by a warrior

indicators.note: inspired is read literally as breathed in, so the son and one go inside the a-plus-warrior letters

parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior
S is the standard abbreviation for son in family trees
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A harsh son who takes his inspiration from a fighting man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspired by' puts SI inside A BRAVE, after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrasive manners grate on people, so the word describes a harsh, rough way of dealing.

clue.text: Tip on new biro replaced? It gains one credit

indicators.note: replaced suggests the letters are put back in different places

explanation.surface: Advice on swapping in a fresh ballpoint, a good deed worth credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' rearranges all twelve letters of TIP ON NEW BIRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Earning favour with someone through a helpful act wins notional credit, the idiom for such approval.

clue.text: Old painter mostly brought up

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means the letters are raised, read from bottom to top
mostly says most but not all of the name is used, dropping its last letter

parts.note: Degas was the French Impressionist painter

explanation.surface: An elderly artist mostly raised in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts DEGAS to DEGA, and 'brought up' reverses that in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Being aged means having lived many years, so it is a synonym of old.

clue.text: European region and African country lecturer disregarded

indicators.note: disregarded says the lecturer's letter is ignored and left out

parts.note: Liberia is a country in West Africa
L stands for lecturer, as in university staff lists

explanation.surface: A lecturer ignores a European region and an African nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disregarded' removes L from LIBERIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberia is the peninsula holding Spain and Portugal, a region of Europe.

clue.text: Mistaken English bishop favoured government

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop
in means popular or favoured, as in the in crowd

explanation.surface: An English bishop backs the government and gets it wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone erring is going astray, making a blunder, so is in the wrong.

clue.text: Observe wise man, we hear, in ancient period

indicators.note: we hear says the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: to eye is to observe, and a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: Watching a sage at work, someone feels transported back to antiquity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns EYE SAGE into its sound-alike, a two-word phrase for a frozen era.
explanation.definitionFit: The glacial epochs of the Pleistocene lie far back in prehistory, a very old stretch of time.

clue.text: One traced by tree favouring a beer when drunk

parts.note: to be for something is to favour it

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters reel about and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A drinker prefers a beer, and gets tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when drunk' rearranges A BEER into EBEAR. The tree is a family tree, so the definition is a person found on it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancestor appears on a family tree, which is what genealogists trace.

clue.text: Park sheep ruined linked to single communications facility

indicators.note: ruined says the letters of these two words are wrecked and rebuilt

parts.note: one is single in number

explanation.surface: Sheep wreck a park, and the incident is reported through a single line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges PARK SHEEP into SPEAKERPH; 'linked to' joins it to ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephone with a loudspeaker lets a group join a call hands-free, a feature of telecoms equipment.

clue.text: Atmosphere created by girl left out

indicators.note: out says the letter for left is dropped from the name

parts.note: Laura is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is ignored and creates a certain atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes L from LAURA.
explanation.definitionFit: An aura is the distinctive feeling or air surrounding a place or person, its atmosphere.

clue.text: Take a view round tree

parts.note: O is round in shape
a pine is a coniferous tree

explanation.surface: Someone forms an opinion while walking around a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state an opinion, to take a particular position on something.

clue.text: Hand, reportedly, for European

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is to be taken as it is heard

parts.note: fin is old slang for a hand

explanation.surface: A hand reportedly working for a European employer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' means the slang FIN is heard as a native of Finland.
explanation.definitionFit: A Finn is a citizen of Finland, a Nordic country, so a European.

clue.text: Study about very old county

indicators.note: about means around, so the study's letters go round the other two

parts.note: a den is a private room or study

explanation.surface: Someone researches a very old English shire.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Devon is one of England's shires, an administrative region.

clue.text: Small amount of money, we hear, for trail

indicators.note: we hear says the coin's name stands for a word that is spoken the same

parts.note: a cent is a coin of tiny value

explanation.surface: Someone is paid a pittance, they say, for following a trail.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunting dog follows the smell an animal leaves behind, which is a trail.

clue.text: Racy valet feverishly hiding dope and source of trips?

indicators.note: hiding says one set of letters is tucked inside the other
feverishly suggests frantic motion, so the letters of these two words are jumbled

parts.note: gen is slang for information, as is dope

explanation.surface: A racy manservant excitedly conceals drugs, which may lead to trips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feverishly' makes TRAVELACY from the two words and 'hiding' holds dope within it. The surface hints at drug trips; the definition means holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: A travel agency books holidays and journeys, so it supplies trips.

clue.text: Elevated quintet gaining a form of congratulation

parts.note: high means elevated
a quintet is a group of five

explanation.surface: A band of five musicians on a raised stage wins applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gaining' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapping raised palms together is a celebratory gesture of praise.

clue.text: Hope lad's cultivated lily

indicators.note: cultivated suggests digging and working, so the letters are turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: A young gardener is hopeful about the lily he has grown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cultivated' rearranges HOPE LAD'S; the possessive gives just S.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphodel is a flowering plant of the lily family, the flower of the Elysian fields.

clue.text: Affluent area represented at heart by losers?

definitions.meaning: the prosperous commuter belt surrounding London
the Conservative heartland, sending MPs from the party that kept losing elections at the time

explanation.surface: A wealthy district whose core voters keep backing the losing side.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties surround London; they were the Conservatives' heartland when the party was out of power after 1997.
explanation.definitionFit: The counties ringing London are known for wealth and safe Conservative seats, the party then in opposition.

clue.text: Wife wears very good cap — who cares?

indicators.note: wears means has on, so the hat letters sit around the wife's letter

parts.note: so, as in the reply just so, signals approval, very good
a cap is a kind of hat

explanation.surface: A wife puts on a fine cap and shrugs off criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wears' means the wife letter sits inside the very-good-plus-cap run, as if wearing it.
explanation.definitionFit: The dismissive retort means it does not matter, a shrug of indifference.

clue.text: A sports car? It's raised a shameful sign

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the whole run of letters is read upwards

parts.note: MG is a classic British sports car marque

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a sports car is a mark of disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reads A MG ITS upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace attached to someone, a badge of shame.

clue.text: German lot tormented in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A German suffers a great deal of torment.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a common German man's name, borne by Bismarck and several emperors.

clue.text: Waste odds before final

indicators.note: before places the odds ahead of the final

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the odds at the off in horse racing
the end is the final part

explanation.surface: Squandering money on betting before the final race.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, the starting price, is the betting odds offered when a race begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To spend money lavishly is to use it up, to waste it.

clue.text: Quiet hotel accommodating a ruler in east

indicators.note: accommodating means giving room to, so a goes inside the letters for quiet and hotel

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A quiet hotel puts up an Eastern monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shah was the monarch of Iran, a ruler in the Middle East.

clue.text: Star from another opera

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A singer moves from one opera to another.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero of a film or story is its principal player, the star.

clue.text: Second sleep break

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: A brief snooze taken during a break.
explanation.definitionFit: To snap something is to break it cleanly.

clue.text: French Protestant to embrace new tune about love

parts.note: to hug is to embrace

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the love letter
new says the word tune is made over in a fresh order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A Protestant hugs a fresh tune about love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns TUNE into UENT, and 'about' puts O inside it to give UENOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Huguenots were Calvinists in sixteenth- and seventeenth-century France, many of whom fled persecution.

clue.text: International body type is mean

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, is an international body
a kind is a type or sort

explanation.surface: A sort of international organisation behaves meanly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unkind is behaving with spite, which is what being mean signifies.

clue.text: A wee tot played with large kitchen item

indicators.note: played with suggests fiddling about, so the letters of these words are reshuffled

parts.note: L is the size label for large

explanation.surface: A small child plays with something big in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played with' rearranges A WEE TOT into TEATOWE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth for drying dishes is a standard piece of kitchen kit.

clue.text: Request made by a learner after a course

indicators.note: after says the a and learner come behind the a and course

parts.note: PPE, philosophy, politics and economics, is a university course
L is the learner plate on a car

explanation.surface: A request is made by a student who has completed a course.
explanation.walkthrough: PPE is the Oxford degree in philosophy, politics and economics.
explanation.definitionFit: An appeal is an earnest plea, a formal request for help or a decision.
